whyThisShow: February 9, 1973 at Maples Pavilion is a landmark night simply because of what the band was premiering: Eyes of the World, Here Comes Sunshine, China Doll, They Love Each Other, Row Jimmy, and Wave That Flag all played live for the first time. One listener noted that "Here Comes Sunshine comes off a lot smoother" than other debuts that night, adding "it sounds like they've been playing this one for a while" [source: 'Here Comes Sunshine comes off a lot smoother. It sounds like they've been playing this one for a while.']. The second-set run of Truckin' into Eyes into China Doll is what the community consistently points to as the heart of the show, with one reviewer still getting "goose bumps 25 years later" from that Eyes performance [source: 'it STILL gives me goose bumps 25 years later to hear how great this performance is']. One reviewer summed up the band's operating level by reaching for the Bill Graham quote: "they're not just the best at what they do, they're the ones who do what they do" [source: 'they're not just the best at what they do, they're the ones who do what they do']. The Casey Jones encore is missing from the best-circulating recording, which one listener noted with some personal relief given their view that it is "probably the most over rated dead song ever" [source: 'i think it is probably the most over rated dead song ever'].
listenFor: The Eyes of the World is the centerpiece — a first-ever performance that listeners consistently describe as sounding seasoned and assured, with one reviewer noting it "sounds like they been playing it for years" [source: 'sounds like they been playing it for years']. The Playing in the Band draws specific praise for creativity, described as "very creative" with "nice jams" [source: 'The Playin is very creative and has nice jams']. In the second set, China Cat into I Know You Rider gets a direct endorsement: "China->Rider smokes!" [source: 'China->Rider smokes!']. The Sugaree from the first set is the song one reviewer was blasting loud enough to convert a self-described Dead-hater in a drive-through line [source: "I've always hated the Grateful Dead, but that sounds so cool! Turn it up again!"]. The soundboard tape has a character one listener called "crunchy" — their best word for a texture they found distinct even among other '73 SBDs [source: 'the "crunchy" sound of the tape---that\'s the best way to describe it I think'].
context: This show falls in the pre-Wall of Sound era of 1973, a period the community broadly regards as one of the band's creative peaks. The recording circulates as a soundboard (identifier: gd73-02-09.sbd.bertha-fink.14939.sbeok.shnf) and has never received an official release, which makes its canonical standing among fans entirely community-driven. The night served as the world premiere for at least six songs that would become staples — Eyes of the World, Here Comes Sunshine, China Doll, They Love Each Other, Row Jimmy, and Wave That Flag — making it one of the densest debut nights in the band's catalog.
funFact: One reviewer gave away their only low-generation copy of this tape to a stranger at a drive-through who had just heard the Sugaree for the first time and immediately started "rocking out to it" [source: 'I ejected the tape and gave it to the chick at the window and asked her to give it to him. I stayed at the exit for a second to make sure she did, and the guy looked over all stoked and honked his horn'].
headline: Eyes of the World born at Stanford, February '73.
